topic: Peptides your body makes: dermcidin, the antibiotic peptide in your sweat. Dermcidin gene isolated 2001 (Schittek et al., Nature Immunology 2001;2:1133, University of Tübingen): specifically and constitutively expressed in sweat glands, secreted into sweat; proteolytically processed 47-aa peptide with broad antimicrobial activity, maintained over broad pH range and high salt resembling sweat. Review (Schittek, J Innate Immun 2012): expressed in eccrine sweat glands, constitutive (not induced by inflammation), processing starts with 48-aa DCD-1L; active against S. aureus, E. coli, E. faecalis, Candida albicans in sweat-like conditions; untypical salt/pH tolerance; Zn2+-induced self-assembly into ion channels proposed; reduced dermcidin peptides in sweat of atopic dermatitis patients.
